description: Loan lifecycle commands, loan API endpoints and Loan COB: throughput, latency and failures. Alert rules for the same series: config/docker/prometheus/etc/rules/fineract-loans.rules.yml.

panels.title: Loan commands / s
panels.description: Submit, approve, disburse and repay commands, all outcomes. Source: fineract_loan_commands_total.

panels.title: Server error ratio
panels.description: Share of loan commands in the selected time range that ended in outcome="server_error". Yellow from 1%, red from 5%, the thresholds of the alerts FineractLoanCommandErrorRatioHigh and FineractLoanCommandErrorRatioCritical.

panels.title: Command p95 (success)
panels.description: 95th percentile of successful loan commands in the selected time range, all four commands together. Yellow from 1 s, red from 2.5 s, the thresholds of FineractLoanCommandLatencyHigh and FineractLoanCommandLatencyCritical. Interpolated inside the SLO buckets 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2.5s, 5s, 10s.

panels.title: Loan API requests / s
panels.description: Requests to /api/v1/loans and every route below it. Source: http_server_requests_seconds_count.

panels.title: COB loans processed
panels.description: Loans whose COB transaction committed in the selected time range: every step returned and the loan is closed for that COB day. For the batch job, and for an inline COB request that is not retried, this is the number of loans closed. When an inline request of more than one chunk fails and is retried, each attempt runs the chunks that had already committed again and counts their loans again, so the value is then higher than the number of loans closed. Source: fineract_cob_loans_processed_total{outcome="success"}.

panels.title: COB loans failed
panels.description: Loans whose COB transaction did not commit in the selected time range. One failed loan rolls back its whole chunk (100 loans by default) and every loan in the chunk is counted, so this can be far more than the number of loans with an error. An inline COB request stops at the first failure and is retried; each attempt counts the loans it had processed. Any value above zero is red; the alert FineractCobLoanFailures fires on the same condition.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Alerts from config/docker/prometheus/etc/rules/fineract-loans.rules.yml that are firing now. The Prometheus Alerts page lists them.

panels.title: Command throughput by command and outcome
panels.description: Commands per second for each command and outcome. All 20 combinations exist from startup; combinations that stay at zero in the time range are hidden.

panels.title: Server error ratio by command
panels.description: Share of each command that ended in outcome="server_error", over all outcomes of that command. The dashed lines are the alert thresholds: 1% warning, 5% critical. Empty while a command has no traffic.

panels.title: Rejection ratio by command
panels.description: Share of each command that ended in outcome="client_error": the request was rejected with a 4xx status. Data integrity and lock failures are mapped to 4xx too, so a database problem shows here. The dashed line is the 25% threshold of the alert FineractLoanCommandRejectionRatioHigh.

panels.title: Command latency p50 by command and outcome
panels.description: Computed from the SLO buckets 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2.5s, 5s, 10s, so a value is interpolated inside one bucket and anything slower than 10 s reads as 10 s. A series appears when its command and outcome are first recorded.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, command, outcome) (rate(fineract_loan_command_execution_seconds_bucket{application=~"$application", command=~"$command", outcome=~"$outcome"}[$__rate_interval]))) >= 0

panels.title: Command latency p95 by command and outcome
panels.description: Computed from the SLO buckets 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2.5s, 5s, 10s, so a value is interpolated inside one bucket and anything slower than 10 s reads as 10 s. The dashed lines are the p95 alert thresholds: 1 s warning, 2.5 s critical (the alerts look at successful commands only).

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, command, outcome) (rate(fineract_loan_command_execution_seconds_bucket{application=~"$application", command=~"$command", outcome=~"$outcome"}[$__rate_interval]))) >= 0

panels.title: Command latency p99 by command and outcome
panels.description: Computed from the SLO buckets 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2.5s, 5s, 10s, so a value is interpolated inside one bucket and anything slower than 10 s reads as 10 s. A series appears when its command and outcome are first recorded.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, command, outcome) (rate(fineract_loan_command_execution_seconds_bucket{application=~"$application", command=~"$command", outcome=~"$outcome"}[$__rate_interval]))) >= 0

panels.title: Commands in the selected time range
panels.description: One row for each command and outcome with at least one command in the time range. Count comes from the counter; mean, p95 and p99 from the timer. A timer series starts at its first sample, so the latency columns are empty for a combination that was recorded only once in the range.

targets.expr: sum by (command, outcome) (increase(fineract_loan_command_execution_seconds_sum{application=~"$application", command=~"$command", outcome=~"$outcome"}[$__range])) / (sum by (command, outcome) (increase(fineract_loan_command_execution_seconds_count{application=~"$application", command=~"$command", outcome=~"$outcome"}[$__range])) > 0)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, command, outcome) (rate(fineract_loan_command_execution_seconds_bucket{application=~"$application", command=~"$command", outcome=~"$outcome"}[$__range]))) >= 0
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, command, outcome) (rate(fineract_loan_command_execution_seconds_bucket{application=~"$application", command=~"$command", outcome=~"$outcome"}[$__range]))) >= 0

panels.title: Slowest command by command and outcome (max)
panels.description: The longest single command Micrometer saw in its recent window (fineract_loan_command_execution_seconds_max). Unlike the percentiles it is not capped at the last SLO bucket, so it shows how slow the slowest command really was.

panels.title: Loan API endpoints (http_server_requests_seconds, uri = route template)
Request rate by route and method
panels.description: Requests per second for each loan route template and HTTP method. The uri label is the Jersey route template, for example /api/v1/loans/{loanId}, never a resolved path. POST /api/v1/loans/{loanId} covers approve, disburse and every other state transition; the loan command panels tell them apart.

panels.title: Latency p95 by route and method
panels.description: Needs the http.server.requests histogram: FINERACT_MANAGEMENT_METRICS_DISTRIBUTION_HTTP_SERVER_REQUESTS=true (the verify-fineract stack sets it) or management.metrics.distribution.slo.http.server.requests. Without buckets this panel is empty; use the mean panel below. The dashed line is the 1 s threshold of the alert FineractLoanEndpointLatencyHigh.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__rate_interval]))) >= 0

panels.title: Mean latency by route and method
panels.description: Mean response time from _sum and _count, so it works without the histogram. The dashed line is the 500 ms threshold of the alert FineractLoanEndpointMeanLatencyHigh.

targets.expr: sum by (method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_sum{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Responses by status
panels.description: Requests per second on the selected loan routes for each HTTP status. A 409 here can be a loan that COB holds locked; such a request never reaches the command service and is not in the loan command meters.

panels.title: 5xx responses without a route
panels.description: Server errors recorded with uri="UNKNOWN", all endpoints. A request that fails before Jersey matches a route, for example because the database is unreachable, has no route template, so it is missing from every panel that selects loan routes and from the loan command meters. A value above zero here while the loan panels go quiet points at such a failure.

panels.title: Loan endpoints in the selected time range
panels.description: One row for each loan route template and method. p50, p95 and p99 need the http.server.requests histogram. 4xx and 5xx are the share of responses with outcome CLIENT_ERROR and SERVER_ERROR.

targets.expr: sum by (method, uri) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_sum{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__range])) / (sum by (method, uri) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__range])) > 0)
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__range]))) >= 0
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__range]))) >= 0
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__range]))) >= 0

(sum by (method, uri) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri", outcome="CLIENT_ERROR"}[$__range])) or sum by (method, uri) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__range])) * 0) / (sum by (method, uri) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__range])) > 0)

(sum by (method, uri) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri", outcome="SERVER_ERROR"}[$__range])) or sum by (method, uri) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__range])) * 0) / (sum by (method, uri) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{application=~"$application", uri=~"$uri"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Loans processed, last 24 h
panels.description: The meters carry no run identifier, because a job execution id is not a bounded label. With the Loan COB job scheduled once a day, the last 24 hours are one run. Only what Prometheus scraped counts: hours for which Prometheus holds no data add nothing. Counts loans whose transaction committed: every step returned and the loan is closed for that COB day. Inline COB calls count too. For the batch job, and for an inline request that is not retried, this is the number of loans closed. A failed inline request of more than one chunk is retried as a whole, and each attempt counts the loans of chunks that had already committed again, so the value is then higher than the number of loans closed.

panels.title: Loans failed, last 24 h
panels.description: The meters carry no run identifier, because a job execution id is not a bounded label. With the Loan COB job scheduled once a day, the last 24 hours are one run. Only what Prometheus scraped counts: hours for which Prometheus holds no data add nothing. Counts loans whose transaction did not commit: a rolled back chunk counts every loan it carried. Such a loan stays on its old COB date until a later run closes it.

panels.title: Loan failure ratio, last 24 h
panels.description: Loans whose transaction did not commit over all loans counted in the last 24 hours. Red from 5%, the ratio of the alert FineractCobLoanFailureRatioCritical (which looks at 30 minutes and also needs more than 150 such loans).

panels.title: COB step time per loan
panels.description: Time spent inside business steps divided by loans counted, closed or not, over the selected time range: what one loan costs in COB, without reading and writing the loan. Attempts that are retried add step time and no loan.

panels.title: Loans processed per run, by outcome
panels.description: Loans counted in each interval (one minute or longer), stacked by outcome. A loan is counted when its transaction completes: success when it committed, failure (red) when it did not. For the batch job, and for an inline COB request that is not retried, success is the number of loans closed. When an inline request of more than one chunk fails and is retried, each attempt counts the loans of chunks that had already committed as success again, so success is then higher than the number of loans closed. A run shows as a block of bars and its size is the sum of the block, shown as Total in the legend. Each bar is the counter now minus the counter one interval ago, which is exact where increase() would estimate; an interval in which the server restarted shows as zero. A loan that is behind by several days is counted once for each COB day.

panels.title: Step executions per second by step
panels.description: How many loans each business step handles per second, both outcomes. During a run every configured step of a job shows the same rate; a step that drops below the others is failing or was reconfigured.

panels.title: Step latency p50 by step
panels.description: Time one business step takes for one loan. Computed from the SLO buckets 5ms, 10ms, 25ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 1s, 5s: a value is interpolated inside one bucket and anything slower than 5 s reads as 5 s. Both outcomes together.

panels.title: Step latency p95 by step
panels.description: Time one business step takes for one loan. Computed from the SLO buckets 5ms, 10ms, 25ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 1s, 5s: a value is interpolated inside one bucket and anything slower than 5 s reads as 5 s. The dashed line is the 250 ms threshold of the alert FineractCobStepLatencyHigh.

panels.title: Step latency p99 by step
panels.description: Time one business step takes for one loan. Computed from the SLO buckets 5ms, 10ms, 25ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 1s, 5s: a value is interpolated inside one bucket and anything slower than 5 s reads as 5 s. Both outcomes together.

panels.title: COB time by step
panels.description: Seconds spent in each step per second of wall time, stacked: where a COB run spends its step time. A value of 2 means two threads are busy in that step.

panels.title: Step failures by step, since server start
panels.description: Running count of step executions that threw, for each step. This meter counts attempts, so a loan that is retried counts each time, unlike the loan counter above. It is the raw counter and not a rate, because a step's failure series is created by its first failure and a rate cannot see that first sample. Every jump is a failure; the count returns to zero when the server restarts.

targets.expr: sum by (step) (fineract_cob_step_execution_seconds_count{application=~"$application", step=~"$step", outcome="failure"}) or sum by (step) (fineract_cob_step_execution_seconds_count{application=~"$application", step=~"$step", outcome="success"}) * 0

panels.title: COB steps in the selected time range
panels.description: One row for each business step. Failures is the running count since the server started, like the panel above, and not limited to the time range. Share of time is the step's part of all step time.

targets.expr: sum by (step) (fineract_cob_step_execution_seconds_count{application=~"$application", step=~"$step", outcome="failure"}) or sum by (step) (increase(fineract_cob_step_execution_seconds_count{application=~"$application", step=~"$step"}[$__range])) * 0
